title: Aryna Sabalenka denies WTA Finals outburst targeted Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina in apology
content:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. — Aryna Sabalenka has issued a statement denying that a mid-match outburst, in which she allegedly cursed about Ukrainians, was directed at WTA Finals opponent Elina Svitolina.

The Ukrainian knocked Sabalenka out of the season-ending championship in the group stage Friday with a 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 victory at Indian Wells Tennis Garden. A day later, Sabalenka posted an apology on social media for “my comment,” which she wrote “was not directed at Elina.”

“I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment. That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended.”

Shortly after the match, a clip circulated on social media in which she was accused of saying “those f–––ing Ukrainians, for f–––’s sake” in Russian. Sabalenka’s voice is not audible in the clip, drowned out by crowd noise and the chair umpire calling the score as she receives tennis balls while preparing to serve.

The WTA has not commented on the clip, nor on Sabalenka’s apology.

Sabalenka, 28, is from Belarus, an ally of Russia in its invasion of Ukraine, which Vladimir Putin launched in 2022. At this year’s Australian Open, Sabalenka said in a news conference, “I want peace, and if I could change anything, I would definitely do that.”

Her comment was in response to Ukrainian player Oleksandra Oliynykova naming Sabalenka among players Oliynykova said had engaged with or praised state-sponsored activities or their countries’ leaders. She alleged that Sabalenka signed a letter supporting Belarus president Aleksandr Lukashenko in 2020, during protests against his regime.

At the 2023 French Open, Sabalenka skipped two news conferences after being repeatedly questioned about her association with Lukashenko. “I don’t support war, meaning I don’t support Lukashenko right now,” Sabalenka said after defeating Svitolina in the tournament’s quarterfinals. They did not shake hands then, nor at the end of their match Saturday, as part of a longstanding policy from Ukrainian players not to shake hands with Russian or Belarusian opponents.

Sabalenka’s season ended with Friday’s loss to Svitolina. Svitolina, 32, went on to beat Wimbledon champion Linda Nosková 6-2, 6-1 in the semifinals in a one-sided victory. She will play Mirra Andreeva, a Russian, in the final Sunday, after the 19-year-old defeated Jessica Pegula of the U.S. 6-3, 6-4.
